messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Sev1 - multi-gpu serving cluster (tp4) - alerts: repeated NCCL communicator hangs + CUDA Xid errors on a subset of nodes. Paging oncall@sre.

alice: I'm on it, acknowledging page. seeing ~8% increase in 5xx on /v1/generate in us-west-2.

rahul: getting logs from the affected pod, container is restarting on OOM after a short stall. kernel log shows a series of `Xid 79` and `GPU page fault` entries.

sre_lead: quick question — any recent infra changes? kernel/driver push last night?

eng-runtime: we rolled a CUDA driver kernel package to the staging fleet at 02:30 UTC and promoted to canary nodes overnight. Looks like 6 nodes in the serving pool got the new driver.

alice: tallying impacted hosts -> gk2-09, gk2-12, gk2-13, gk2-21. All on same driver version `525.105.17+patch`.

rahul: here's the stack we see repeatedly in the container logs before restart:
```
[2026-03-15T02:44:11Z] NCCL WARN Call to `ncclCommInitRank` failed: unhandled exception
[2026-03-15T02:44:11Z] RuntimeError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure (loading kernel)
[2026-03-15T02:44:11Z] aborting, killing process to recover
```

eng-runtime: also seeing `ncclCommDestroy` followed by `transport error - rdma:peer reset` in the fabric logs.

alice: customer impact: intermittent failures for customers on tp4 models; error rate spike correlated with node set above. Keeping traffic to other regions unaffected.

katie-custops: flagged top 5 customers receiving degraded responses, sending initial status email with a 30m ETA for mitigation.

sre_lead: mitigation plan in order of speed: 1) cordon + drain affected hosts, 2) stop scheduling new tp4 jobs on canary driver nodes, 3) increase routing weight to single-gpu model variants as fallback for critical routes, 4) if needed rollback driver on those hosts.

alice: starting drain on gk2-09 and gk2-12 now. pulling `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.

ops-bot: Deploy: cordon gk2-09 true (user: alice)
ops-bot: Drain started for gk2-09, 3 pods evicted, 2 pods rescheduled to healthy nodes.

rahul: evicted pods showed the same crash signature when restarted on different hosts with the new driver. suggests driver/firmware combo is the root cause, not just hardware.

eng-runtime: can we set `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on the runtime to force fallback from NVLink/IB collectives to ring algorithm? That reduces perf but may avoid the communicator deadlock.

sre_lead: yes, do that on the serving pool asap for canary driver nodes only. Update config and rolling restart pods on those nodes.

alice: applying env change to the deployment for the canary node pool: `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` and `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1`. Triggering rolling restart for pods on gk2-12 and gk2-13.

rahul: quick log after restart shows no immediate `ncclCommInit` failures on the restarted pod, token latency is up but error rate dropped back to baseline for those pods.

katie-custops: sending updated customer note: "We have routed traffic away from nodes showing instability and applied a temporary runtime configuration to reduce multi-GPU collectives while we investigate. You may see slightly higher latency for tp4 endpoints; request routing has prioritized availability."

eng-runtime: we're also going to temporarily prefer single-GPU model variants for the highest SLA accounts to avoid cross-node collectives until drivers are fully validated. Routing change pushed to the load balancer.

sre_lead: next steps: 1) continue draining remaining canary driver hosts, 2) escalate to infra team to evaluate rollback of driver package, 3) capture full kernel oops and FABRIC traces for RCA.

alice: handing off paging to rahul (next on-call). rahul, I'm leaving notes in the incident doc and adding a TODO to confirm rollback plan.

rahul: ack, taking over. monitoring error rate and node stability. will coordinate with infra for driver rollback if we see recurrences after env changes.

eng-runtime: FYI we've already reproduced a repro in staging by applying the exact driver + firmware combo and running a tp4 microbenchmark — it triggers an inter-GPU hang inside NCCL's allreduce under certain tensor alignment patterns.

sre_lead: good repro. capture the NCCL logs with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL`, and gather `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DEBUG` outputs from affected hosts.

rahul: collecting traces now; if infra approves rollback I'll coordinate rolling that to the 4 affected hosts only.

katie-custops: advised sales/customer success to expect a follow-up with a postmortem and ETA for permanent remediation.

ops-bot: Alert autoscaler: shifted 20% more traffic to warm pool in us-west-2 (policy: emergency-fallback).

rahul: status update: error rate down to baseline after env changes and routing adjustments. still collecting debug artifacts.

sre_lead: great work. keep the incident open until we have either a driver rollback or vendor confirmation. Also schedule a blameless RCA with eng-runtime + infra + SRE.

alice: adding incident tags: `nccl`, `driver-regression`, `multi-gpu`, `sevpager`. I'll draft the timeline once we close.

rahul: handing off to night oncall who is on the `sre_night` rotation at 03:30 UTC. leaving clear runbook: if errors recur -> rollback driver on affected hosts -> cordon -> drain -> revert routing.

katie-custops: sent final customer follow-up at 03:05 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident S1 updated: status=mitigated, impact=partial, assignee=rahul, link=https://redwood.internal/incidents/2839012345

sre_lead: thanks team. postmortem owners: eng-runtime (root cause & fix), infra (driver rollout process), SRE (runbook improvements).

ash: (note left in thread for visibility) please capture which model prompt lengths triggered the repro — the tp4 microbenchmark indicated long sequence lengths + uneven tensor splits make the collectives fragile.

rahul: noted. attaching repro logs to the incident page and closing this slack thread when artifacts are uploaded.

alice: closing handoff. good job everyone :thumbsup:
